deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. Gauss is building tables, prime by prime, for p ≡ 1 (mod 8). For each p he works with the class group of binary forms (a,b,c) = ax²+2bxy+cy² of determinant b²−ac = −p, i.e. modern discriminant −4p. The next page groups these primes by class number: 4 | 17, 73, 97, 193; 8 | 41, 313, …; 40 | 761, 881.

TABLE LAYOUT. Each table has a header {0 1 2 … / h, h−1, …} pairing each index k with h−k. 'Cl. k. h−k' then denotes a class and its inverse, where class k is the k-th power of a generating class. For both 761 and 881 the generator is the class of the form (3,1,(p+1)/3). Cl.0 is the principal class; Cl.h/2 is the ambiguous class of order 2.

NOTATION ON EACH LINE. The entry 'c.N' (or 'c.N(B)') gives the reduced form (N,±B,·) of that class.
- The parenthesised number is the middle coefficient. It is written when two classes share the same first coefficient, e.g. 15(2) vs 15(7), and 21(8) vs 21(1).
- The written sum of squares is the representation p = x²+y²+z² that belongs to that class.
- How a representation gives a class (Disq. Arith. §§278–292): restrict x²+y²+z² to the lattice orthogonal to the primitive vector w = (x,y,z). This is a positive binary form of determinant w·w = p, i.e. Gauss determinant −p.
- Example: for 22²+19²+6² = 881, the vector u = (2,−2,−1) ⟂ w has norm 9, so the class is (9,±1,98) = class ±2.
- Only the even (principal-genus) classes receive representations. Their number matches r3(p) = 12h(−4p) [my statement of the standard identity].

(1) p = 761, h = 40 (end of the previous page's table).
- Cl.16.24: 761 = 21²+16²+8². Here u = (0,1,−2) ⟂ w has norm 5, so the class is (5,2,153).
- [Mine, check] Generator f = (3,1,254). Then f² = (9,−2,85), f⁴ = (10,3,77), f⁸ = (25,8,33). f¹⁶ = f⁸·f⁸: B ≡ 8 (25) and B² ≡ −761 (625) give B = 308, and (625,308,153) reduces to (5,2,153). This confirms c.5.
- Cl.18.22: 761 = 22²+14²+9², with c left blank. [Mine] f¹⁸ = f¹⁶·f² = (45,7,18), which reduces to (18,−7,45), so the blank should be 18.
- Cl.20: 761 = 27²+4²+4², c.2, the ambiguous class (2,1,381).
- Count check: the previous page has 7 three-square representations (classes 2–14), plus 16 and 18 here, giving 9. Then 48·9 + 24 (from 20²+19²) + 24 (from 27²+2·4²) = 480 = 12·40, consistent with h = 40.

(2) p = 769: only a skeleton. h = 20, pairs Cl.k.20−k, Cl.10 self-inverse. No computations.

(3) p = 809: only a skeleton. h = 32, pairs k, 32−k, up to Cl.16.

(4) p = 857: only a skeleton. h = 32, pairs k, 32−k.

(5) p = 881, h = 40.
- The header originally paired k with 36−k (36 struck out). The inverse indices in the Cl lines are struck through by a vertical stroke, and '40' is written beside 881. The margin pairs '11.29', '12.28' are the corrected inverses.
- [Mine] Powers of f = (3,1,294), obtained by lifting √−881 mod 3^k and reducing:
  - f = (3,1,294); f² = (9,1,98).
  - f³ = (27,−8,35).
  - f⁴: (81,46,37) reduces to (26,9,37).
  - f⁵: (243,127,70) reduces to (15,2,59).
  - f⁶: (729,370,189) reduces to (5,2,177).
  - f⁷ = (15,7,62); f⁸ = (21,8,45); f⁹ = (7,1,126); f¹⁰ = (21,1,42).
  - f¹¹ = (14,−1,63); f¹² = (25,12,41); f¹³ = (30,−7,31); f¹⁴ = (10,3,89).
  - f¹⁵ = (30,13,35), which matches the next page; f²⁰ = (2,1,441); f²¹ = (6,1,147).
- Gauss's entries:
  - Cl.0: 25²+16².
  - Cl.1 c.3; Cl.2 c.9 with 22²+19²+6²; Cl.3 c.27; Cl.4 c.26 with 24²+17²+4²; Cl.5 c.15(2).
  - Cl.6 c.5 with 26²+13²+6²; Cl.7 c.15(7); Cl.8 c.21(8) with 28²+9²+4²; Cl.9 c.7.
  - Cl.10 c.21(1) with 19²+18²+14². All of these agree with my powers.
  - The main-column lines labelled 11 (c.30.7) and 12 (29²+6²+2², c.10) are actually f^±13 and f^±14.
  - In the margin Gauss supplies the true 11 (c left blank; it is (14,∓1,63), odd, so no representation) and 12 (20²+16²+15², c.25 = (25,12,41)).
- Orthogonal-vector checks:
  - 26²+13²+6²: u = (1,−2,0), norm 5.
  - 28²+9²+4²: u = (1,−4,2), norm 21.
  - 19²+18²+14²: u = (2,1,−4), norm 21.
  - 29²+6²+2²: u = (0,1,−3), norm 10.
  - 20²+16²+15²: u = (3,0,−4), norm 25.
- Over this page and the next, the even classes 2,4,…,18 each receive exactly one three-square representation; 0 gets the two-square one and 20 gets 9²+20²+20². That is 9 representations, and 48·9 + 24 + 24 = 480 = 12·40.

PURPOSE. These are empirical tables of cyclic class-group structure and of the three-squares ↔ principal-genus correspondence for p ≡ 1 (mod 8). They feed the next page's sorting of primes by h(−4p) (all multiples of 4 here).

'64 302' at the bottom is an unexplained number.
errors: 881 table: the main-column entries labelled Cl.11 (c.30.7) and Cl.12 (841+36+4, c.10) belong to classes ±13 = (30,−7,31) and ±14 = (10,3,89) under the generator (3,1,294). Gauss had skipped classes 11 = (14,−1,63) and 12 = (25,12,41). The marginal '11.29 c:' and '12.28 400+256+225 c:25' supply them; the c for class 11 is left blank.
881 table: the inverse indices were first computed against a wrong class number (36). They were struck out and replaced by 40.
761: c for Cl.18 (484+196+81) is left blank; it should be 18, since the reduced form is (18,∓7,45).
The c entries omit the sign of the middle coefficient, so class k and its inverse 40−k are not distinguished. This is harmless because they are listed as a pair.

results.what: Class groups of determinant −p (disc −4p) for p = 761 and 881 are cyclic of order 40, generated by (3,1,(p+1)/3); explicit reduced forms are given for each power. Skeleton tables are set up for 769 (h=20) and 809, 857 (h=32).
results.modern_name: Structure and class numbers of imaginary quadratic class groups Cl(−4p); cycle of a generating form under composition
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801; class-number tables in Werke II)

results.what: Assignment of each representation p = x²+y²+z² to a class of the principal genus, via the form on the lattice orthogonal to (x,y,z). The count of representations matches r3(p) = 12h(−4p).
results.modern_name: Gauss's three-squares theorem / correspondence between primitive representations by sums of three squares and binary form classes

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine numerical class-group and three-squares bookkeeping of a kind Gauss is well known to have done (DA §291f., class-number tables in Werke II). The only interest is the visible correction of a skipped pair of classes in the 881 table.

checkable.asserts: The three-square representations of 761 on the page are correct.

Lifted square roots of −881 mod 3^k used for the powers of (3,1,294).
Each listed c(B) defines a form of determinant −881.
Orthogonal vectors of norms 9, 10, 25, 21 confirm the c values 9, 10, 25, 21(1).
Composition step showing f^16 = (5,2,153) for p = 761 (c.5).

transcription_corrections: Beside 881 Gauss wrote '40', the corrected class number. The original header's second row began with 36, which is struck out.
In the 881 table the second (inverse) index of every 'Cl.k.' line is struck through by a long vertical stroke. The transcription's [-36-], [-35-], … rendering is right in substance.
The marginal lines '11.29 c:' and '12.28. 400+256+225 (c:25' are corrections inserted for classes 11 and 12, not continuations of the list.
Cl.4 in the 881 table: the last summand '16' is heavily overwritten; it reads 576+289+16.
